name: Purpose
summary: The reader sees at once what you want from them. State the purpose early and expand on it later, usually near the end.
checklist: The purpose is clear in the opening lines.
The request is expanded on later in the letter.
The reader does not have to search for what you are asking.

name: Content
summary: Include everything this reader needs to continue care, and report the case notes accurately.
checklist: All key information for continuing care is there.
Facts from the notes are accurate: doses, dates, results.
The detail suits what this reader already knows.

name: Conciseness & Clarity
summary: Leave out what the reader does not need and summarise the case clearly.
checklist: No irrelevant details copied from the notes.
The case is summarised, not listed line by line.
Length is about 180–200 words.

name: Genre & Style
summary: A clinical, factual, professional letter suited to the reader. Use technical terms and abbreviations only as far as this reader will follow them.
checklist: Factual tone, no personal feelings or judgements.
Professional register throughout.
Fewer abbreviations and more explanation for a GP or another specialty; plain words if the patient will read it.

name: Organisation & Layout
summary: Logical paragraphs, key information easy to find, and a clear layout.
checklist: Paragraphs follow a logical order.
Key information stands out and is not buried.
The letter does not simply follow the order of the case notes.
The layout is clear.

name: Language
summary: Accurate grammar, vocabulary, spelling and punctuation that never get in the way of meaning.
checklist: Spelling and punctuation are correct.
Longer sentences are grammatical too.
Word choice is precise.

name: Intelligibility
summary: You are easy to understand: clear sounds, stress, intonation and rhythm.
checklist: Key words and medical terms are pronounced clearly.
Stress and intonation help the listener.
Your accent does not make you hard to follow.

name: Fluency
summary: Speech flows at a normal speed without long searches for words.
checklist: Normal speaking speed.
Few pauses to search for words.
Little repetition or self-correction.

name: Appropriateness of Language
summary: Register, tone and words suit a conversation with a patient; technical matters are explained in lay terms.
checklist: Plain words instead of jargon.
A polite, respectful tone.
Explanations the patient can follow.

name: Resources of Grammar and Expression
summary: A wide, flexible range of grammar and vocabulary, used accurately.
checklist: Varied sentence structures.
Accurate grammar in longer sentences.
Natural, idiomatic expressions where they fit.

name: Relationship building
summary: Start well and stay respectful, non-judgemental and empathic.
checklist: Greet, introduce yourself and explain the purpose.
Stay attentive and respectful.
Do not judge the patient.
Acknowledge feelings and worries.

name: Understanding and incorporating the patient's perspective
summary: Find out the patient's ideas, concerns and expectations, and use them.
checklist: Ask about ideas, concerns and expectations.
Notice and respond to the patient's cues.
Link your explanations to what the patient told you.

name: Providing structure
summary: A purposeful, logical conversation with clear signposting.
checklist: Work through the task in a logical order.
Signpost when you change topic.
Organise explanations: first…, then…, finally…

name: Information gathering
summary: Let the patient talk, move from open to closed questions, clarify and summarise.
checklist: Listen actively; don't interrupt.
Open questions first, then closed ones.
No leading or double questions.
Clarify vague answers.
Summarise so the patient can correct you.

name: Information giving
summary: Give information in small chunks, checking what the patient knows, feels and understands.
checklist: Ask what the patient already knows.
Give information in small chunks and pause.
Invite the patient's reactions.
Check understanding.
Ask what else they would like to know.
